## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
In generation 0, all 84 trials scored 0 on dev and also 0 on training, across every network family and recipe tried. So the agent is failing to learn at all, not failing to generalise, and seed noise cannot be measured yet. The starting network can already represent a simple correct rule: place a brick where the 'missing' channel is set at the column's current height. The bottleneck is therefore more likely learning dynamics (for example the policy settling on an early DONE because random placements are net negative, or too few useful updates) or a quirk of this world, than missing capacity. In round 1 I will spread risk across three untested directions: (1) recipe settings never tried (lr 3e-3, 512 parallel worlds, gae_lambda 0.8); (2) a much smaller network with as many samples as the budget allows (1 epoch, 1024 worlds); (3) a zero-initialised learned layer that can remap action logits, to test whether the action layout in this world differs from the one described.

### Round 2
All 87 trials so far, including this round's untried recipe, a tiny network and a learned action remap, scored 0 on both dev and training. Seed noise still can't be measured, and no idea can be ranked against another. The capacity, recipe and layout-remap explanations all look weak. One cause has not been tested: the exact-build bonus. Exactness needs two things: an unbroken run of precise placements, and a DONE choice at exactly the moment the build is complete. Early in training, DONE at a random time ends the episode and loses fill reward, so DONE is probably pushed down hard. The complete state is also rarely seen. Meanwhile, sloppy big bricks earn more discounted shaped reward than careful ones. So I'm testing: (1) long-horizon credit assignment that keeps the +1 bonus in view; (2) a dedicated, easy-to-learn DONE detector built on the missing and extra channels; (3) learned spatial mixing over the whole grid, a family not tried yet, in case target and build are related across distant cells.

### Round 3
Every trial so far has scored 0, in training and on dev, so seed noise cannot be measured and no idea can be ranked against another. All of them failed the same way, whatever the network or recipe, so I suspect a failure in learning itself rather than one in capacity or layout. My leading guess, which has not been tested directly, is that the agent learns to end every episode at once. Early random placements fill more cells outside the target than inside it, so they earn negative return, while DONE earns 0. PPO would then quickly push up the DONE logit, episodes would shrink to near zero length, and the agent would never learn to fill. A DONE bias of -2 only delays this by a few hundred Adam steps. With Adam, multiplying the DONE logit by a fixed small factor should slow its growth about tenfold and keep episodes long. This round gives this idea three tests: the bare scaling, scaling with more samples, and scaling with a structured DONE detector.

### Round 4
All 9 trials in this search scored 0 on dev and 0 on training, the same as the 84 trials in generation 0. Learning fails completely, not just generalisation. Several things are now ruled out as the cause on their own: very high lr, many parallel worlds, gae_lambda 0.8, a tiny network, near-Monte-Carlo returns, a learned action remap, a separate DONE detector, a slowed DONE logit, direct paths from the missing cells, and token mixing. Seed noise still can't be measured. Either this world differs from its description (for example sparse reward or different mechanics), or exploration never finds a learnable signal. In the last round I'll make three bets on things never tried: (1) many small gradient steps with clip 0.3; (2) standard PPO initialisation (orthogonal weights, near-uniform starting policy) with the highest allowed entropy; (3) multiplicative per-column features, so that 'missing at the landing layer' can be represented in one step.
